correctness.rationale: Capping the discrete counts and then ignoring marks for completed players leaves the finishing order unchanged. Poisson thinning and a common rescaling give independent Gamma(i, rate i) times for goals i=1,2,n, with no ties. Independently, for s>0, integrating 4x exp(-sx) above the third completion time and taking expectation gives 4 r_s(1/s^2+n/[s(n+s)]), where r_s=(n/(n+s))^n. Subtract the s=3 integral from s=2 to recover (2); expanding the product of the first two CDFs gives (1). The differences in (3) follow. An independent exact dynamic program in reviews/evidence-4-race.py used only the original discrete race: at residual state d, condition on the next active mark, choosing i with probability goal_i divided by the sum of active goals. It reproduced all three formulas at all 498 integers 2 through 499 and checked both required strict margins and the exact n=2 fractions and tie. For n>=500, the logarithmic inequalities bound r_c between exp(-c) and exp(-c)/(1-c^2/(2n)); both signs and coefficient extrema in (6)-(7) give the stated lower bounds. Independent rational Taylor bounds and fraction comparisons reproduce 20931734927/2484922590000 > 1/200 and 114949/10353000 > 1/100. This analytic tail, not finite extrapolation, completes the quantifier.
residual_risks: No optimal-gap, arbitrary-triple, or noninteger-shape claim is validated.
